london/pub-history-walk.title: Pub History Walk
london/pub-history-walk.description: Start early to beat the crowds — Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese is best savoured before the after-work rush. Wear comfortable shoes; the cobblestones between Southwark and Wapping can be uneven.

venues.name: Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese
venues.activityDescription: A literary icon rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1666. Dickens, Twain, and Dr. Johnson all drank here. Order a pint of real ale and explore the labyrinthine cellar bars.

venues.name: The Lamb and Flag
venues.activityDescription: Tucked down an alley in Covent Garden, this 17th-century pub was once nicknamed the 'Bucket of Blood' for its bare-knuckle fights. Try the guest cask ales.

venues.name: The George Inn
venues.activityDescription: London's last surviving galleried coaching inn, now owned by the National Trust. Shakespeare may have performed in the cobbled courtyard. Sit in the oak-panelled rooms.

venues.name: The Prospect of Whitby
venues.activityDescription: London's oldest riverside pub, dating to 1520. Smugglers and pirates once drank here. Grab a window seat overlooking the Thames for golden hour views.

london/hidden-shoreditch.title: Hidden Gems of Shoreditch
london/hidden-shoreditch.description: Shoreditch is best on weekdays when the crowds thin out. The street art changes constantly, so keep your eyes peeled for fresh pieces on every visit.
london/hidden-shoreditch.query: Hidden gems of Shoreditch East London

venues.name: Brick Lane Street Art Tour
venues.activityDescription: Wander the backstreets around Brick Lane and Hanbury Street for world-class street art — Banksy, Stik, and ROA all have pieces here. Don't miss the murals in Shoreditch Yard.

venues.name: Rough Trade East
venues.address: Old Truman Brewery, 91 Brick Ln, London E1 6QL
venues.activityDescription: London's legendary independent record shop inside the Old Truman Brewery. Browse vinyl across every genre, catch an in-store gig, and grab a flat white from their in-house café.

venues.name: Dishoom Shoreditch
venues.activityDescription: Bombay-inspired café famous for its black daal and bacon naan roll. The Shoreditch location in a converted warehouse has the best atmosphere of any branch.

venues.name: Columbia Road Flower Market Area
venues.activityDescription: Even on non-market days, Columbia Road is lined with quirky independent shops — vintage furniture, artisan ceramics, and specialty delis tucked behind colourful shopfronts.

london/royal-parks.title: Royal Parks & Gardens
london/royal-parks.description: Pack a light picnic from a nearby deli — the parks have wonderful benches and lawns. In spring the rose gardens are stunning; in autumn the colours along the Serpentine are magical.

venues.name: The Serpentine & Italian Gardens
venues.activityDescription: Start at the ornamental Italian Gardens at the head of the Serpentine. Walk along the lake past the Peter Pan statue and the Serpentine Gallery pavilion.

venues.name: Kensington Palace & Orangery
venues.activityDescription: Stroll through Kensington Gardens to the palace grounds. Stop at The Orangery for an elegant morning tea with scones, surrounded by 18th-century architecture.

venues.name: Queen Mary's Rose Garden
venues.address: Regent's Park, Chester Rd, London NW1 4NR
venues.activityDescription: London's largest collection of roses with over 12,000 plants. Walk the circular paths, enjoy the fragrance, and find a bench by the lake for a quiet moment.

venues.name: Primrose Hill
venues.activityDescription: Climb to the top for one of London's best panoramic views — the entire skyline from the Shard to the BT Tower stretches before you. Perfect for photos.

london/best-coffee-zone1.title: Best Coffee in Zone 1
london/best-coffee-zone1.description: Most specialty shops here are busiest 8-10 AM on weekdays. Go mid-morning for the best experience and freshest pour-overs.

venues.name: Monmouth Coffee
venues.activityDescription: Borough Market's beloved roaster since 1978. Queue for their single-origin filter coffee and a fresh pastry. The beans are roasted just around the corner.

venues.name: Prufrock Coffee
venues.activityDescription: Founded by World Barista Champion Gwilym Davies. A temple of specialty coffee with a training lab upstairs. Try their espresso tasting flight.

venues.name: Kaffeine
venues.activityDescription: An Aussie-run café that consistently ranks among London's best. Their flat whites are textbook-perfect, and the avocado toast is worth the hype. Great brunch spot.

venues.name: Rosslyn Coffee
venues.activityDescription: A sleek specialty café near the Royal Exchange. Known for their precision-pulled espressos and rotating single-origin beans from top micro-roasters.

london/thames-sunset.title: Thames Sunset Walk
london/thames-sunset.description: Check sunset time before heading out and plan to be at the Millennium Bridge area during golden hour. The South Bank is best walked east to west so the light is always in front of you.
london/thames-sunset.query: Thames sunset walk South Bank London

venues.name: Tower Bridge Viewpoint
venues.activityDescription: Start at the south side of Tower Bridge for iconic views. Walk along the Queen's Walk past City Hall and the Scoop amphitheatre.

venues.name: Tate Modern Terrace
venues.activityDescription: Head to the free viewing terrace on Level 10 for sweeping views across the Thames to St Paul's Cathedral. The light here during golden hour is extraordinary.

venues.name: Southbank Centre Food Market
venues.activityDescription: Street food from around the world right on the riverbank. Grab a bite, find a bench facing the river, and watch the sunset paint the sky over Westminster.

venues.name: Westminster Bridge Sunset
venues.activityDescription: End at Westminster Bridge for the postcard view — Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament lit up against the fading sky. One of London's most romantic moments.

nyc/brooklyn-brunch.title: Brooklyn Brunch
nyc/brooklyn-brunch.description: Go early on a Saturday — the best brunch spots in Williamsburg hit peak wait times by 11 AM. Take the L train to Bedford Ave to start.
nyc/brooklyn-brunch.query: Brooklyn brunch crawl Williamsburg to DUMBO

venues.name: Devoción
venues.activityDescription: Colombian-sourced beans roasted on-site in a stunning greenhouse-style space. Their cold brew is legendary. The atrium fills with natural light in the morning.

venues.name: Five Leaves
venues.activityDescription: The late Heath Ledger's passion project. Famous for their ricotta pancakes with honeycomb butter and the Moroccan scramble. Sidewalk seating is prime people-watching.

venues.name: McCarren Park
venues.activityDescription: Walk through Williamsburg's favourite park. On weekends there's often a farmers market or pickup soccer. A perfect digestive stroll between courses.

venues.name: Juliana's Pizza
venues.activityDescription: Patsy Grimaldi's triumphant return — coal-fired thin-crust perfection under the Brooklyn Bridge. Get the classic margherita and a seat with bridge views in DUMBO.

nyc/speakeasy-circuit.title: Speakeasy Circuit
nyc/speakeasy-circuit.description: Reservations are essential for PDT and Angel's Share. Most speakeasies have a 'no standing' policy, so arrive ready to wait for a seat. Dress smart-casual.

venues.name: Please Don't Tell (PDT)
venues.address: 113 St Marks Pl, New York, NY 10009
venues.activityDescription: Enter through the phone booth inside Crif Dogs hot dog shop. The original NYC speakeasy revival spot. Order the Mezcal Mule and soak in the wood-panelled intimacy.

venues.name: Angel's Share
venues.activityDescription: Hidden behind an unmarked door inside a Japanese restaurant. Intimate Japanese-influenced cocktail bar with exquisite presentation. No parties larger than four.

venues.name: Attaboy
venues.activityDescription: No menu, no sign outside — just a buzzer on an unmarked door. Tell the bartender what flavours you like and they'll create something bespoke. The spiritual successor to Milk & Honey.

venues.name: Employees Only
venues.activityDescription: Behind a psychic's neon sign in the West Village. Award-winning cocktails served by bartenders in white coats. The late-night kitchen serves excellent bone marrow.

nyc/rooftop-sunset.title: Rooftop Sunset Tour
nyc/rooftop-sunset.description: Check sunset time and plan to reach your second stop 30 minutes before. Most rooftop bars have cover charges after dark — arrive before sunset to skip them.

venues.name: Westlight
venues.activityDescription: Perched atop The William Vale hotel in Williamsburg with 360-degree views of the Manhattan skyline. The craft cocktails match the vistas. Start here for afternoon light.

venues.name: 230 Fifth Rooftop Bar
venues.activityDescription: Directly facing the Empire State Building from its massive rooftop. The golden hour light hitting the ESB from here is unbeatable. In winter they provide robes and igloos.

venues.name: Bar SixtyFive at Rainbow Room
venues.activityDescription: 65 floors above Rockefeller Center with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Central Park and the skyline. Art Deco elegance meets jaw-dropping views. Dress code enforced.

venues.name: Mr. Purple
venues.activityDescription: End the night on the Lower East Side with a pool-deck rooftop overlooking downtown Manhattan. The energy shifts from chill to party as the night goes on.

nyc/chinatown-little-italy.title: Chinatown to Little Italy
nyc/chinatown-little-italy.description: Come hungry — this is a serious food walk. Chinatown is better for authentic food; Little Italy is more about atmosphere. The transition between the two happens in just one block.
nyc/chinatown-little-italy.query: Chinatown Little Italy food walk Manhattan

venues.name: Nom Wah Tea Parlor
venues.activityDescription: NYC's oldest dim sum parlor, open since 1920 on the Bloody Angle of Doyers Street. Order the original egg roll and the shrimp and snow pea leaf dumplings.

venues.name: Mott Street Markets
venues.activityDescription: Walk Mott Street and Canal Street for Chinese bakery stops — egg tarts, pineapple buns, and boba tea. Duck into the herbal shops and fish markets for the full sensory experience.

venues.name: Rubirosa
venues.activityDescription: Cross into Little Italy for vodka-sauce pizza at Rubirosa — thin, crispy, and widely considered one of the best slices in the city. The tie-dye vodka pie is the move.

venues.name: Ferrara Bakery & Café
venues.activityDescription: The grand dame of Little Italy since 1892. End with a cannoli and an espresso in the ornate café. Their pistachio cannoli and tiramisu are the perfect sweet finish.

nyc/museum-marathon.title: Museum Marathon
nyc/museum-marathon.description: The Met alone could take days — set a time limit or pick one wing before going. Friday evenings the Met stays open late and is wonderfully empty.

venues.name: MoMA
venues.activityDescription: Start with the heavy hitters — Starry Night, Campbell's Soup Cans, Les Demoiselles d'Avignon. Don't miss the sculpture garden. Two hours is tight, so pick 2-3 floors max.

venues.name: Neue Galerie
venues.activityDescription: A gem of Austrian and German art in a stunning Beaux-Arts mansion. Klimt's gold 'Portrait of Adele' is worth the visit alone. The café downstairs serves excellent Viennese pastries.

venues.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
venues.activityDescription: The crown jewel. Head straight to the Egyptian Temple of Dendur, the European paintings, or the rooftop garden (seasonal). The rooftop bar has Central Park views.

venues.name: Whitney Museum of American Art
venues.activityDescription: Renzo Piano's striking building in the Meatpacking District. The outdoor terraces offer High Line and Hudson River views. End your day with contemporary American art and sunset.

boston/harbor-seafood.title: Harbor Seafood Trail
boston/harbor-seafood.description: The best lobster is in season from June through December. Order your chowder 'New England style' (cream-based) — never Manhattan style in this town.

venues.name: Yankee Lobster Co.
venues.activityDescription: A family-run fish market turned restaurant right on the Seaport waterfront. Their lobster roll is piled high with fresh claw meat, lightly dressed with butter. No frills, just perfection.

venues.name: Row 34
venues.activityDescription: An industrial-chic oyster bar in the Innovation District. Try a dozen East Coast oysters with a rotating selection from Island Creek and other New England farms. Pair with a local IPA.

venues.name: Neptune Oyster
venues.activityDescription: Tiny, legendary North End seafood spot. The hot butter lobster roll here is considered the best in Boston. No reservations, so time your visit strategically.

venues.name: Legal Harborside
venues.activityDescription: Three floors of seafood on the harbor. Hit the rooftop (Floor 3) for sunset cocktails and fried clam strips overlooking Boston Harbor and the skyline.

boston/academic-roast.title: Academic Roast
boston/academic-roast.description: Cambridge cafés fill up when classes let out around 3 PM. Morning visits are quieter and better for finding a study nook. Walk through Harvard Yard between stops.
boston/academic-roast.query: Specialty coffee tour Cambridge MA Harvard MIT

venues.name: Broadsheet Coffee Roasters
venues.activityDescription: A serious micro-roaster near Harvard with beans sourced directly from farms. The light, airy space is perfect for a quiet morning pour-over. Try their rotating single-origin.

venues.name: 1369 Coffee House
venues.activityDescription: A neighbourhood institution since 1993. Mismatched furniture, local art on the walls, and the kind of place where someone is always writing a thesis. Their chai latte is beloved.

venues.name: Tatte Bakery & Café
venues.activityDescription: Israeli-inspired bakery near Kendall Square/MIT. The shakshuka and halva croissant are destination-worthy. Beautiful, bright interior with communal tables.

venues.name: Dado Tea
venues.activityDescription: A tranquil tea house steps from Harvard Square. Over 100 loose-leaf teas from around the world. The matcha latte and tea-infused pastries are a gentle counterpoint to all the coffee.

boston/cobblestone-romance.title: Cobblestone Romance
boston/cobblestone-romance.description: Beacon Hill is at its most atmospheric after dusk when the gas lamps flicker on. Wear heels at your own risk — the cobblestones are charming but treacherous.

venues.name: Toscano
venues.activityDescription: A charming Italian spot on Beacon Hill's main street. The weekend brunch with fresh pasta and mimosas is the perfect start. Sit in the window and watch Charles Street go by.

venues.name: Acorn Street
venues.activityDescription: The most photographed street in America — tiny cobblestoned lane with gas lamps, flower boxes, and Federal-style brick homes. Step through the looking glass into 1820s Boston.

venues.name: Boston Public Garden
venues.activityDescription: America's first public botanical garden. Take a ride on the iconic Swan Boats, walk across the suspension bridge, and find the Make Way for Ducklings statues.

venues.name: Yvonne's
venues.activityDescription: A glamorous speakeasy-style supper club in a former Locke-Ober space. Velvet booths, craft cocktails, and shareable plates in one of Boston's most atmospheric rooms.

boston/freedom-trail-remix.title: Freedom Trail Remix
boston/freedom-trail-remix.description: The red brick line on the sidewalk is your guide — just follow it. Mike's vs. Modern Pastry is the great Boston debate. Try both and pick a side.
boston/freedom-trail-remix.query: Freedom Trail with food stops Boston

venues.name: Boston Common & State House
venues.activityDescription: Start where the Freedom Trail begins. Walk past the golden dome of the Massachusetts State House. The Common is America's oldest public park, established in 1634.

venues.name: Mike's Pastry
venues.activityDescription: The legendary North End cannoli stop. Grab a lobster tail pastry or a pistachio cannoli from the blue box. The line is part of the experience.

venues.name: Old North Church
venues.activityDescription: Where the 'one if by land, two if by sea' lanterns were hung in 1775. The oldest standing church in Boston. Step inside the white box pews.

venues.name: Bunker Hill Monument & Craft Beer
venues.activityDescription: Climb all 294 steps to the top of the obelisk for panoramic views. Then reward yourself at a nearby Charlestown brewery or craft beer bar.

boston/fenway-day.title: Fenway Day Out
boston/fenway-day.description: Buy tickets early — Fenway is the smallest park in MLB and sells out often. Bleacher Bar opens at 11 AM and fills up fast on game days. Arrive early.
boston/fenway-day.query: Fenway Park game day experience Boston

venues.name: Eastern Standard
venues.activityDescription: A Kenmore Square institution for pre-game brunch. Classic American brasserie with a legendary cocktail program. The raw bar and steak frites are game-day fuel.

venues.name: Bleacher Bar
venues.activityDescription: Built into the center field wall of Fenway Park itself. Grab a stool at the garage-door window and watch batting practice through the opening. Truly one-of-a-kind.

venues.name: Fenway Park
venues.activityDescription: America's Most Beloved Ballpark since 1912. Sit near the Green Monster, grab a Fenway Frank, and sing 'Sweet Caroline' in the 8th inning. Nothing else like it.

venues.name: Cask 'n Flagon
venues.activityDescription: The original Red Sox post-game bar since 1969. Packed with fans reliving the game over craft beers and burgers. The energy after a Sox win is electric.

austin/live-music-crawl.title: Live Music Crawl
austin/live-music-crawl.description: Most venues don't charge cover on weeknights. Check venue websites for set times — headliners usually go on around 10 PM. Bring earplugs for the smaller rooms.

venues.name: The Continental Club
venues.activityDescription: The crown jewel of Austin's live music scene since 1957. Blues, rockabilly, and country in an intimate room on South Congress. No cover most nights — just walk in and be amazed.

venues.name: Mohawk
venues.activityDescription: Three stages in the heart of the Red River Cultural District. The outdoor rooftop stage under the stars is quintessential Austin. Catch local and touring indie acts nightly.

venues.name: la Barbecue
venues.address: 2401 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
venues.activityDescription: Fuel up between sets with some of Austin's best brisket. The line is shorter than Franklin's but the quality rivals it. Get the beef rib if they haven't sold out.

venues.name: Rainey Street Bungalow Bars
venues.activityDescription: End the night hopping between converted house bars on Rainey Street. Each bungalow has its own vibe — craft cocktails at Lustre Pearl, frozen drinks at Bungalow, live DJs at Container Bar.

austin/taco-trail.title: Taco Trail
austin/taco-trail.description: Breakfast tacos are a religion in Austin — locals have strong opinions. Veracruz and Tacodeli are the two camps. Try both and choose your allegiance wisely.
austin/taco-trail.query: Taco tour Austin breakfast to late night

venues.name: Veracruz All Natural
venues.address: 1704 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
venues.activityDescription: The migas taco here might be the single best breakfast item in Austin — crispy tortilla strips, eggs, cheese, and verde salsa in a fresh flour tortilla. Life-changing.

venues.name: Tacodeli
venues.activityDescription: The Otto (refried black beans, bacon, avocado) is legendary. Their Doña salsa is so popular they sell it by the jar. A slightly more refined breakfast taco experience.

venues.name: Valentina's Tex Mex BBQ
venues.activityDescription: The genius collision of Texas BBQ and Tex-Mex. The Real Deal Holyfield taco — smoked brisket, eggs, cheese, and salsa in a homemade tortilla — is a must. Worth every minute in line.

venues.name: Torchy's Tacos (South Congress)
venues.activityDescription: The OG location that started the Torchy's empire. Ask for the secret menu — 'The Matador' with jamaican jerk chicken and mango is incredible. Browse South Congress shops after.

austin/keep-austin-weird.title: Keep Austin Weird
austin/keep-austin-weird.description: The Congress Avenue bats emerge at dusk from March to October — check the bat hotline for emergence times. The Cathedral of Junk requires an appointment.
austin/keep-austin-weird.query: Keep Austin Weird quirky spots tour

venues.name: Greetings from Austin Mural
venues.activityDescription: The iconic vintage postcard-style mural on South First. The morning light is best for photos without harsh shadows. Austin's most Instagrammed wall.

venues.name: Uncommon Objects
venues.activityDescription: A sprawling vintage bazaar with 24 dealer booths full of taxidermy, neon signs, antique medical equipment, and curiosities you never knew you needed. Gloriously weird.

venues.name: Castle Hill Graffiti Wall
venues.activityDescription: The legal graffiti park where the art changes daily. Layer upon layer of spray paint creates a constantly evolving outdoor gallery. Bring a can and add your own mark.

venues.name: Congress Avenue Bridge Bat Colony
venues.activityDescription: 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats emerge at dusk in one of nature's most spectacular urban phenomena. Watch from the bridge or the kayaks below. Arrive 30 min before sunset.

austin/east-side-coffee.title: East Side Coffee
austin/east-side-coffee.description: East Austin mornings are best before the heat kicks in. Most cafés here have generous patios — perfect for the cooler morning hours. Street art changes between visits.

venues.name: Flat Track Coffee
venues.address: 1619 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
venues.activityDescription: A motorcycle-themed micro-roaster in a converted garage. Their espresso is punchy and their cold brew is dangerously smooth. The tiny patio feels like a secret club.

venues.name: Cenote
venues.address: 1010 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
venues.activityDescription: A beautiful converted bungalow with a sprawling oak-shaded patio. Known for excellent pour-overs and a brunch menu featuring migas and avocado toast. East Austin's living room.

venues.name: Figure 8 Coffee Purveyors
venues.activityDescription: Clean, modern space with windows overlooking Chicon Street. Their rotating selection of guest roasters keeps things interesting. The cortado here is textbook.

venues.name: Merit Coffee
venues.activityDescription: San Antonio's beloved roaster opened this East Austin outpost with a slick, modern bar. Their house blend is approachable; their single-origins are for the adventurous.

austin/lady-bird-lake.title: Lady Bird Lake Day
austin/lady-bird-lake.description: Bring sunscreen — there's very little shade on the water. Weekday mornings are quietest for paddleboarding. Barton Springs is a refreshing 68°F year-round.
austin/lady-bird-lake.query: Lady Bird Lake outdoor day Austin

venues.name: Pfluger Pedestrian Bridge
venues.activityDescription: Start on this pedestrian bridge spanning Lady Bird Lake for sweeping views of the downtown skyline reflected in the water. The morning light here is gorgeous for photos.

venues.name: Texas Rowing Center Kayak Rental
venues.address: 1541 W Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78703
venues.activityDescription: Rent a kayak or paddleboard and glide across the calm, no-wake waters of Lady Bird Lake. Watch turtles sunbathe on logs and herons fish along the shore.

venues.name: Barton Springs Pool
venues.activityDescription: A spring-fed pool that stays 68°F year-round. Three acres of crystal-clear water surrounded by pecan trees. Austin's most beloved natural swimming hole — a true local treasure.

venues.name: Hula Hut
venues.activityDescription: A Polynesian-Tex-Mex fusion spot built over the water on Lake Austin. Sit on the deck with your feet practically in the lake. The fish tacos and frozen margaritas hit different here.

paris/cafe-culture.title: Café Culture
paris/cafe-culture.description: Always sit facing the street — it's the Parisian way. A café crème is the morning drink; espresso is for after lunch. Tipping isn't required but rounding up is polite.
paris/cafe-culture.query: Café culture tour Paris best cafés

venues.name: Café de Flore
venues.activityDescription: Where Sartre and de Beauvoir held court for decades. Order a café crème and a croissant at the same terrace where existentialism was born. The Art Deco interior hasn't changed since the 1930s.

venues.name: Coutume Café
venues.activityDescription: Paris's third-wave coffee pioneer. A bright, Scandinavian-style space serving perfectly extracted single-origins. The contrast with the classic cafés makes you appreciate both traditions.

venues.name: Café La Palette
venues.activityDescription: An artist hangout since 1902, tucked between the galleries of Rue de Seine. Cézanne and Picasso once drank here. The zinc bar and painted tile murals are magnificent.

venues.name: Boot Café
venues.address: 19 Rue du Pont aux Choux, 75003 Paris
venues.activityDescription: A former cobbler's shop turned tiny specialty coffee bar in the Marais. Barely fits 6 people inside — grab your flat white and sit on the steps outside. Perfectly Parisian.

paris/hidden-marais.title: Hidden Marais
paris/hidden-marais.description: The Marais is best explored slowly. Most shops close on Sundays except along Rue des Rosiers (the Jewish quarter). Push open any heavy door — there's often a courtyard behind it.
paris/hidden-marais.query: Hidden gems Le Marais Paris walking tour

venues.name: Place des Vosges & Hôtel de Sully
venues.activityDescription: Paris's oldest planned square, built by Henri IV in 1612. Walk through the secret passage of Hôtel de Sully — push through the heavy door at #62 and emerge into the Renaissance courtyard.

venues.name: L'As du Fallafel
venues.activityDescription: The legendary falafel of Rue des Rosiers. Order the 'spécial' — a pita overflowing with crispy falafel, aubergine, hummus, and tahini. Eat it standing up like a local.

venues.name: Musée Carnavalet
venues.activityDescription: Paris's history museum, completely free, housed in two Renaissance mansions. Proust's reconstructed bedroom, Revolutionary artefacts, and Roman-era boats from the Seine.

venues.name: Merci Concept Store
venues.activityDescription: Paris's most stylish concept store in a converted fabric factory. Three floors of curated fashion, homewares, and books. Their café in the basement uses library reading room as its theme.

venues.name: Le Mary Celeste
venues.activityDescription: End with natural wines and fresh oysters at this buzzy Marais wine bar. The bartenders' cocktails are equally excellent. Sit at the marble bar and watch the neighbourhood wind down.

travelTimes.from: Place des Vosges & Hôtel de Sully

paris/seine-sunset.title: Seine at Sunset
paris/seine-sunset.description: Buy a bottle of wine from a caviste on the Left Bank and join the locals sitting along the quais at dusk. Check sunset time and start 3 hours before.
paris/seine-sunset.query: Seine sunset walk Paris Notre-Dame to Eiffel Tower

venues.name: Île de la Cité
venues.activityDescription: Start at the tip of the island behind Notre-Dame at Square du Vert-Galant, where the Seine splits in two. The oldest willow tree in Paris shades this romantic triangle of parkland.

venues.name: Left Bank Bouquinistes
venues.activityDescription: Browse the iconic green riverside bookstalls that have lined the Seine since the 16th century. Hunt for vintage prints, old maps, and secondhand books while the golden light builds.

venues.name: Pont Alexandre III
venues.activityDescription: Paris's most ornate bridge, dripping with gilded cherubs and Art Nouveau lampposts. Time your crossing for golden hour — the light on the gold is otherworldly.

venues.name: Trocadéro Esplanade
venues.activityDescription: The definitive Eiffel Tower sunset view from across the Jardins du Trocadéro. Watch the tower catch the last light, then sparkle on the hour after dark. Pure cinematic Paris.

paris/patisserie-trail.title: Pâtisserie Trail
paris/patisserie-trail.description: French pâtisseries sell out of popular items by afternoon. Visit the artisan shops before noon for the best selection. Small portions — this is a marathon, not a sprint.

venues.name: Du Pain et des Idées
venues.activityDescription: Christophe Vasseur's legendary bakery near Canal Saint-Martin. The pain des amis and the escargot pistache-chocolat are transcendent. Arrive when they open — the croissants sell out.

venues.name: Cédric Grolet Opéra
venues.activityDescription: Sculpted fruit-shaped pastries that are almost too beautiful to eat. Each one is a masterpiece of trompe-l'oeil. The lemon and the hazelnut are works of art — literally.

venues.name: L'Éclair de Génie
venues.activityDescription: Christophe Adam reinvented the humble éclair into jewel-like confections. The yuzu-passion fruit and the salted caramel are standouts. Each one is a glossy, architectural wonder.

venues.name: Pierre Hermé
venues.activityDescription: The 'Picasso of Pastry.' His Ispahan macaron (rose, lychee, raspberry) changed French pastry forever. Buy a box of macarons for the train home.

venues.name: Angelina
venues.activityDescription: End in this Belle Époque salon de thé that's been serving Paris since 1903. Their Mont-Blanc (chestnut cream vermicelli over meringue) and legendary thick hot chocolate are the perfect finale.

paris/montmartre-bohemian.title: Bohemian Montmartre
paris/montmartre-bohemian.description: Take the funicular up to Sacré-Cœur to save your legs for the backstreets. Avoid the portrait artists at Place du Tertre — walk the quieter streets behind instead.
paris/montmartre-bohemian.query: Bohemian Montmartre artistic walking tour Paris

venues.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
venues.address: 35 Rue du Chevalier de la Barre, 75018 Paris
venues.activityDescription: Start at the top of the butte for the best panorama in Paris — on clear days you can see 50 kilometres. The white Romano-Byzantine basilica glows in the morning light.

venues.name: Musée de Montmartre
venues.activityDescription: Renoir's former studio, now a museum of Montmartre's artistic golden age. The gardens overlook the last vineyard in Paris. Utrillo, Suzanne Valadon, and the cancan come alive here.

venues.name: La Maison Rose
venues.activityDescription: The pastel-pink restaurant on the corner of Rue de l'Abreuvoir — one of the most photographed buildings in Paris. Have lunch on the terrace overlooking the cobbled lane.

venues.name: Place des Abbesses & Le Mur des Je t'aime
venues.activityDescription: End at the charming village square. Visit the 'Wall of Love' — 311 tiles with 'I love you' written in 250 languages. Browse the independent boutiques and have a final glass of wine.

travelTimes.to: Place des Abbesses & Le Mur des Je t'aime
